cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. As junior coordinator, you're responsible for the blocked sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran the whole event yesterday. You said I'd earned a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. To senior coordinator. Still below me, but now you can supervise the plumber.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can only come after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll lock up too. I can't give building security to a junior.

mechanism: A grants a promotion that remains below personal rank and uses the new title to attach more unwanted responsibility.
confusable: D49 seeks help as service; D53 specifically pushes unwanted responsibility downward, so the burden and relative rank must be clear.
comparison: A blocked sink and late plumber lead to lockup duty; the inspector alternative uses representation and signature responsibility.
seedUse: The existing D53-a still-below-me promotion already turns superior status into the instrument of downward assignment.
